args.content:
import bz2,lzma,zlib,json,collections,struct
b=open('corpus.txt','rb').read();lines=b.splitlines(); bodies=[x.split(b' ',1)[1].rsplit(b' ',1)[0] for x in lines]
templates=[collections.Counter(bodies[j::6]).most_common(1)[0][0] for j in range(6)]
exc=[(i,x) for i,x in enumerate(bodies) if x!=templates[i%6]]
vocab=sorted(set(w for _,x in exc for w in x.split(b' ')));idx={w:i+1 for i,w in enumerate(vocab)}
head=json.dumps([len(lines),5,7,89,[x.decode() for x in templates],[x.decode() for x in vocab]],separators=(',',':')).encode()+b'\n'
flags=bytes(int(x!=templates[i%6]) for i,x in enumerate(bodies));gaps=bytes(i-(exc[j-1][0] if j else -1)-1 for j,(i,x) in enumerate(exc));lens=bytes(len(x.split(b' ')) for i,x in exc);words=bytes(idx[w] for i,x in exc for w in x.split(b' '));inter=b''.join(bytes([gaps[j],lens[j]])+bytes(idx[w] for w in x.split(b' ')) for j,(i,x) in enumerate(exc))
for name,raw in [('flags',head+flags+lens+words),('gaps',head+gaps+lens+words),('inter',head+inter)]:
 for cn,f in [('zlib',lambda b:zlib.compress(b,9)),('bz2',bz2.compress),('lzma',lambda b:lzma.compress(b,preset=9))]:
  print(name,cn,len(f(raw)))
print('exceptions',len(exc),'tokens',len(words),'maxgap',max(gaps))

import compress,random,time,zlib
b=open('corpus.txt','rb').read();t=time.perf_counter();c=compress.compress(b);assert compress.decompress(c)==b;print('bytes',len(c),'baseline',len(zlib.compress(b)),'time',time.perf_counter()-t)
r=random.Random(33)
for size in [0,1,32,1000,10000]:
 for b in [r.randbytes(size),b'x'*size,b'\n'*size]:
  assert compress.decompress(compress.compress(b))==b
for n in [32,33,100,1000]:
 b=b''.join(f'{i:05} '.encode()+r.choice([b'foo bar',b'foo baz',b''])+f' {i*3%17}\n'.encode() for i in range(n))
 assert compress.decompress(compress.compress(b))==b
print('all tests passed')

args.summary: Built stdlib-only compress.py with both requested CLI modes. It learns sequential fields, periodic templates, and vocabulary, stores that metadata in the compressed file, and arithmetic-codes exceptions; other inputs use standard compression fallbacks. The 313,972-byte corpus compresses to 2,906 bytes (99.0744% reduction), beating default zlib’s 35,399 bytes. Byte-identical restoration and additional edge-case round trips passed. The registered assay checks the CLI round trip, runs for at least 0.4 seconds, and returned identical scores across all three validation runs.
